A Marathon Reunion
Maria Lawrence
I stood at the starting line, surrounded by a sea of runners stretching and
chatting nervously.
I took a deep breath and tightened my shoelaces・Today's
marathon was special -
I was running fbr an old friend
l hadn't seen in five
years.

Jenny and
l met on the first day of university and bonded over our shared
passion for running.
From then on, we trained together, pushing each other to
be better.
Running was a bond that kept us close.
However, things changed
just after graduation during our final marathon together.
Every summer, the

Suddenly, I felt a new hope and excitement for the race.
◆◆◆◆◆
As the starting gun fired,
I pushed forward, my feet hitting the road in
rhythm with my racing heartbeat.
I tried to focus, but memories of the past
wouldn't leave me
alone.
Back in university｡Jenny had always been faster.
She was the one who set our running goals, the one who encouraged me
to
train harder.
When l was close to giving up, Jenny would find a way to make
me laugh and keep me going.
We were more than just friends - we were
teammates who believed in each other.
The cheering crowd pulled me back to the present.
I was nearing the
halfway point of the marathon - the same point where Jenny had been injured
five years ago.
My legs felt heavy, but
l kept pushing forward, driven by the
hope of finding my old friend waiting at the finish line
l didn't know if Jenny

◆◆◆◆◆
Nearing the final stretch of the marathon, my muscles ached, and every
breath was a struggle, but
l kept running.
This marathon felt longer than any
I had run in the past, but the memory of Jenny's smile and the note in my
pocket kept me going.
I wondered what l would say if Jenny really was at the
finishline・Should
l apologize？Should lthank herfor evervthing？
These
confusing thoughts made my steps heavier.
As the finish line came into view,
I
felt another rush
of emotions.
The
crowd was cheering loudly, but
l couldn't hear their voices over the sound of
my own heartbeat.
I crossed the line, breathing heavily, and looked around,

We hugged and the last five

◆◆◆◆◆
That evening, we went to dinner to catch up.
Jenny told me how much

regretted not responding

Now,
I began to understand how hard

Jenny told me that after the accident, she visited our old training ground every
year and
thought
about our time
together remembering my
last
message
written on the card.
Then earlier this year, she was sitting on our favorite
bench reading the university's newsletter・She saw an article about the local
marathon, and
it had pictures from the
last ten years.
There, in one
of the
photos, was me and Jenny crossing the finish line.
It was the first time we ran
a marathon together.
Jenny took this as a sign.
That
is when she wrote a
message on the bench and the flyer.
◆◆◆◆◆
－⑥－22－

It has been two years since that wonderful reunion. Jenny and l visit each
other often.
We talk or video chat nearly every day.
The doctor said Jenny
could start training again.
And that brings us to now.
Jenny and
l
are
standing at the starting line of a short 5km charity run.
After all this time,
Jenny and
l discovered an important lesson.
We shouldn't worry too much
about the past. Every day is a new starting line.
